prompt_prefix: Examples from other databases (these tables are NOT in the target database):
Schema: CREATE TABLE customer (customer_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE orders
(order_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, amount REAL);
Question: Which customers have orders totaling more than 100 dollars?
SQL: SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, SUM(o.amount) AS total_amount FROM customer c JOIN orders o ON
o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name HAVING SUM(o.amount) > 100 ORDER BY
Schema: CREATE TABLE book (book_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT); CREATE TABLE loan (loan_id
INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, book_id INTEGER, returned_date TEXT);
Question: Which books have an unreturned loan?
SQL: SELECT b.book_id, b.title FROM book b WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM loan l WHERE l.book_id =
b.book_id AND l.returned_date IS NULL) ORDER BY b.book_id;
Return exactly one read-only SQLite SELECT query (WITH is allowed). Return SQL only, without
Markdown. Use the exact target table names.

questionResults.question: How many pantries are in each city?
questionResults.sql:
SELECT a.city, COUNT(p.pantry_id) AS pantry_count
FROM pantry p
JOIN adress a ON p.address_id = a.address_id
GROUP BY a.city;
questionResults.friendlyResponse: Denver: 1 pantry, Phoenix: 1 pantry, Provo: 1 pantry.

questionResults.question: What is the total quantity of food in each pantry, including shelves and cupboards?
questionResults.sql:
SELECT p.pantry_id, SUM(s.quantity + c.quantity) AS total_quantity
FROM pantry p
LEFT JOIN shelfs s ON s.pantry_id = p.pantry_id
LEFT JOIN cupboards c ON c.pantry_id = p.pantry_id
GROUP BY p.pantry_id
ORDER BY p.pantry_id;
questionResults.friendlyResponse: Pantry 1 has a total quantity of 47. Pantry 2 has a total quantity of 22. Pantry 3 has a total quantity of 20.
